reviews.core_assessment: Independently read218-245 and811-938 before the selector rationale. Path reversal preserves peb(v)+out(v): its source gains a pebble and loses one outgoing arc, its target does the reverse, and each intermediate vertex retains outgoing degree. Summing gives the subset conservation identity. Only acceptance of an internal edge decreases peb(Vprime)+out(Vprime). Choose i as the largest adjacent occupied layer index in Vprime, which attains l(Vprime) by monotonic L; then the source three cases exhaust all internal accepted edges. At layer i the acceptance threshold leaves l_i pebbles; at i-1 an unused vertex in layer i+1 contributes k_(i+1); at earlier layers the two unused vertices contribute k_i+k_(i+1). For the converse, Reach(u) union Reach(v) has out=0 and no later-layer vertices; the unaccepted internal edge makes the sparsity comparison strict. Conservation forces more than l_i pebbles in this reachability union. If the endpoints have at most l_i, an external reachable pebble exists, and a simple path reversal increases their combined count by1, even if the other endpoint is an internal path vertex. Repeating finitely accepts the edge.

standard_prerequisites.name: Finite directed-graph reachability and depth-first search
standard_prerequisites.statement: Reach(v) is the set of vertices accessible by directed paths, and can be found by depth-first search.
standard_prerequisites.use: Find a path bringing one pebble to an endpoint; no sparsity or matroid theorem is assumed.

core_obligations: Identify and establish conservation of pebbles plus outgoing edges for vertices and subsets.
Prove the lower bound on pebbles plus boundary edges despite layer-dependent sparsity thresholds, separating current, immediately preceding, and earlier edge layers.
For a sparse graph, use the closed union of the two endpoint reachability sets and the still-missing edge to force an available external pebble.
Show that repeated path reversals increase the pebble count at the two endpoints until the edge is accepted; combine with the invariants for both recognition directions.

proof_roadmap.step: Establish all four invariants. The nonconstant threshold is controlled by edge-processing order and the two strict parameter inequalities.
Convert the subset invariant into sparsity, and total conservation into tightness.
Under the explicitly stated sparse-graph premise, the endpoint reachability set has no outgoing edge and contains a missing edge; conservation gives a strict pebble surplus.
Iterate the reachability move to accept every edge.

approved_task_config.difficulty_reason: The substantive obligation is a correctness proof for a layered extension of the pebble game with different sparsity deficits at different ranks. Conservation alone is insufficient: the invariant must exploit the processing order and distinguish three layer cases, then be combined with a closed reachability-set obstruction to force progress. No matroid structure, surplus-independence lemma, or correctness of an earlier pebble game is supplied as a shortcut.
